title: Adding, Subtracting, Multiplying and Dividing Functions
short: Combine functions and find the domain of the result.
trouble: Students forget that (f/g)(x) is undefined where g(x) = 0.

blocks.html: Functions are rules that make numbers, so you can add, subtract, multiply and divide them the same way you combine numbers. You already add and subtract polynomials (Adding and Subtracting Polynomials); here the polynomials have names.

$(f + g)(x) = f(x) + g(x)$, $(f - g)(x) = f(x) - g(x)$, $(fg)(x) = f(x)\,g(x)$ and $\left(\frac{f}{g}\right)(x) = \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}$. The domain is every $x$ where both $f$ and $g$ are defined, and for $\frac{f}{g}$ you also remove every $x$ with $g(x) = 0$.

To find $(f + g)(3)$ you need $f(3)$ and $g(3)$, so both rules must accept the input 3. If either refuses it, the combination can't be computed. Division adds one more refusal, because dividing by 0 has no answer.

blocks.name: graph
blocks.cap: The dashed curve $h$ is $f + g$: its height at any $x$ is the height of $f$ plus the height of $g$. Read a column of the table to see it.

blocks.title: Subtracting functions
steps: The minus sign reaches every term of $g$: $2x + 3 - x^2 + 1$.
Combine and write in standard form: $-x^2 + 2x + 4$.

blocks.title: The domain of a quotient
blocks.q: With the same $f$ and $g$, find the domain of $\frac{f}{g}$.
steps: $f$ and $g$ are polynomials, so both accept every real number.
Remove the zeros of $g$: $x^2 - 1 = 0$ when $x = 1$ or $x = -1$.

blocks.title: A root and a denominator together
blocks.q: Let $f(x) = \sqrt{x}$ and $g(x) = x - 4$. Find the domain of $\frac{f}{g}$.
steps: $g(x) = 0$ at $x = 4$, which is inside $[0, \infty)$, so take it out.

blocks.html: Forgetting that $\frac{f}{g}$ is undefined where $g(x) = 0$, especially after simplifying. With $f(x) = x^2 - 4$ and $g(x) = x - 2$, the quotient simplifies to $x + 2$, but the domain still leaves out $x = 2$, because $g(2) = 0$. Always find the domain from the original $f$ and $g$, before you simplify.
